_comment: BI-35 golden file for share allocation.
The DIP's test-plan line is 'golden files for share rounding to exactly 100', and that is
what this pins. Two kinds of case:
exact  - inputs whose shares are determined by arithmetic alone, whatever the rounding
policy is, so the expected list can be written down honestly.
sums   - awkward inputs where the individual shares depend on the largest-remainder rule.
Only the invariant is asserted: the shares add up to exactly 100, which is the
property the screen depends on and the one a naive round-each-independently
Writing expected per-element values for the second group would pin the current algorithm
rather than the requirement, and would have to be rewritten the next time it is tuned.

exact.name: a single category takes all of it
a category with nothing in it gets nothing

sums.name: three equal thirds, the classic case that rounds to 99.9
the design's seventeen categories, all different
amounts that differ by a cent
a long tail of very small shares
